newsitem.title: USA: Dollar lower in U.S. as trading winds down in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dollar lower in U.S. as trading winds down in 1996.

text.p: The dollar fell against most major currencies on the final trading day of the year, pressured by a sell-off in stocks and bonds, experts said.

Stocks and bonds tumbled after news that new home sales rose at the fastest level in nearly four years in November and consumer confidence jumped in December. Yet traders played down the price action which came in very light volume as trading wound down early before Wednesday's New Year holiday.
"You have to keep in mind too that liquidity is so thin that this move is exaggerated," said Brian McCarthy, a market analyst at Ruesch International.
"But essentially, it was the stocks and bonds that got things started," said McCarthy, referring to the dollar declines.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed more than one point lower to yield 6.64 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial average slid nearly 50 points in late afternoon.

The dollar had climbed to a fresh 45-month high of 116.40 yen in Europe before the surprisingly strong U.S. numbers hit the market. At 1400 EST/1900 GMT, the dollar stood at 116.03/13 yen, down from 116.15/25 yen at the open.
The dollar fell to 1.5395/05 marks at 1400 EST/1900 GMT, down sharply from 1.5510/20 at the open.
The dollar decline against the German currency was exacerbated by the mark's gains against the yen, according to traders.
The mark traded around 75.25/30 yen in late dealings, up from about 75.08/11 in mid-morning flows.
Sterling soared on Tuesday to $1.7163, its highest level in more than four years.
At 1400 EST/1900 GMT, sterling stood at $1.7120/30, up from $1.7013/23 at the open.

The British currency gained amid expectations that interest rates in Britain are headed higher next year and as investors rushed to purchase pounds before the new year, experts said. The pound's rise accelerated as pre-set orders to buy were triggered when the currency hit key technical levels.
"There was clearly some year-end buying going on today that drove this thing higher in very thin markets," said Bob Near, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Bank of New York.
It is the anticipation of the rate hike, said Ben Strauss, an assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer and Co.
"But, I think it's way over done," said Strauss, referring to the British currency rally on Tuesday.
In an interview with a French newspaper last week, Bank of England Governor Eddie George said Britain may need to raise rates before the next general election to prevent the economy from overheating.
Elsewhere, the dollar stood at 1.3395/05 Swiss francs at 1400 EST/1900 GMT, down from 1.3475/85 at the open. The dollar was little changed at Canadian $1.3700/10 versus C$1.3701/06.
The Australian dollar traded around $0.7945/52 in late afternoon, down from $0.7953/58 at the open.
